transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, it’s probably nothing too serious, but I’ve noticed I’m having a little trouble when people are talking to me. Like at the museum, someone will be telling me about the next art walk, and I’m looking right at them, trying to listen, but then I realize I missed the middle part of what they said. I end up asking them to run it by me again. I just thought maybe I should check whether that’s… you know, something worth looking into.
Do you have any trouble hearing people when they talk to you, or is it more that you just can't seem to follow what they're saying?

I don’t think it’s my hearing, really. It’s more like… I’ll be looking right at them, like when someone at the museum is telling me about the next art walk, and I’m trying to listen, but somehow I miss the middle of what they said. Then I have to ask them to run it by me again. It’s not all the time, I don’t think, but enough that I noticed it.
Do you think you're having trouble paying attention to what's being said, or do you think you're just not understanding it when you do hear it?

I think it’s more paying attention than understanding. I mean, if I catch what they say, it makes sense. It’s just that someone at the museum will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’m looking at them, trying to listen, and then I realize I missed the middle part. Then I have to ask them to run it by me again. I hope that makes sense.
Does this trouble with paying attention happen every day or just sometimes?

I wouldn’t say it’s every day, exactly… or at least I don’t notice it every day. It’s more just sometimes, like at the museum when someone’s talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’m looking at them, but then I realize I missed the middle part and have to ask them to go over it again. It’s not terrible, I don’t think, but it’s happened enough that I wondered if I should mention it.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently?

I’m not really sure… I don’t think I’ve noticed a big problem with that. I mean, I might forget little things here and there, like anyone, but nothing recent stands out to me as a serious issue. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you have trouble following instructions or completing tasks?

A little, yes… not in a way that I mean to ignore things. If someone gives me a few things to handle for the volunteer group, I’ll usually do the first part, like printing the maps, and then I might forget the next piece, like calling the museum desk. Or I’ll leave the folders kind of half-ready until someone reminds me. It’s not all the time, but it does happen.
Are these difficulties with paying attention and following instructions causing any problems for you at work or in your daily activities?

A little bit, yes… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but with the museum group, I think they’ve started quietly giving some of the planning parts to other people instead of me. Nobody’s been unkind about it, but I notice it.

And I’ve… I guess I don’t feel as confident leading the art walks as I used to. I worry I’ll miss something or not keep things straight. Does that count as a problem in daily activities?
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family due to these difficulties with paying attention and following instructions?

I don’t think so, not in any big way. My family and friends haven’t really said anything to me about it, at least not that I can think of.

Maybe there are small moments where someone has to remind me of something, but I wouldn’t say it’s changed the relationship. I hope that’s answering what you’re asking.
Have you been feeling anxious or depressed about these difficulties with paying attention and following instructions?

I wouldn’t say depressed, no. Maybe a little worried or embarrassed when I realize I missed a step, but I try not to dwell on it too much. It’s more like, “Oh, I should’ve done better with that,” and then I hope nobody thinks badly of me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling sad or down because of these difficulties with paying attention and following instructions?
No, I don’t think I’ve been feeling sad or down because of it. Maybe a little disappointed in myself sometimes, but not really sad, if that makes sense. I try to just correct it and move on.
Have you noticed these difficulties with paying attention and following instructions happening consistently over time?

Yes, I think so. It hasn’t been forever, exactly, but it’s been pretty noticeable for… maybe about two years and a few months now.

It seemed to start causing more trouble after my friend died and I ended up taking over the museum liaison duties by myself. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but since then I’ve had to pay more attention to instructions and details on my own, and that’s when it became more obvious. Does that answer what you mean by consistently over time?
Are these difficulties significantly impacting your ability to perform daily tasks or maintain your current lifestyle?

I guess… yes, somewhat. I wouldn’t want to say I can’t manage day to day, because I still do. But with the museum group, they’ve sort of quietly moved some of the planning parts away from me, which is probably for the best, but it doesn’t feel great.

And I’ve stopped feeling as confident leading the art walks like I used to. I still try, but I’m more hesitant now. So yes, it is affecting things, just… maybe not in a dramatic way. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any changes in how you interact with others or if they treat you differently because of your trouble with paying attention and following instructions?

A little, yes. I don’t think anyone’s been unkind to me or anything like that, but I can tell the museum group has sort of… quietly taken some planning pieces off my plate. They don’t make a big issue of it, which I appreciate, but I notice it.

And I’ve stopped feeling as confident leading the art walks the way I used to. I’m more careful, maybe more hesitant. So I guess it has changed things some, just not in a dramatic way. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you felt like your trouble with paying attention and following instructions has affected your friendships or relationships with family members?

Not really, no… at least not that I’ve noticed in a clear way. My family hasn’t said anything, and I don’t think friendships have changed much because of it.

I suppose I might be a little more careful or apologetic sometimes, but I wouldn’t want to blame that on attention issues unless someone else noticed it too. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had to make any significant adjustments to your daily routine or work responsibilities due to these difficulties with paying attention and following instructions?

Yes… I suppose I have, though I wouldn’t call it a huge formal change. With the museum group, some of the planning parts have kind of been shifted away from me quietly. Nobody made a big announcement or anything, and honestly it may be better that way, but I do notice it.

And with the art walks, I still help, but I don’t feel as confident leading them like I used to. I’m a bit more hesitant now. So yes, there have been adjustments… maybe more than I’d like to admit. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you experienced any other symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness in your body?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed numbness or tingling or weakness like that. At least nothing that stands out to me. Is that what you were asking?
Have you experienced any head injuries or concussions in the past?
No, not that I can think of. I don’t remember having a concussion or any serious head injury. Nothing that I’d say was significant, anyway.
Have you experienced any seizures or loss of consciousness?
No, I don’t believe so. I’ve never had a seizure that I know of, and I can’t recall passing out or losing consciousness. Nothing like that has happened, as far as I’m aware.
Have you experienced any changes in your speech or language abilities, such as difficulty finding the right words or following conversations?

Not really speech, I don’t think—I can talk okay. It’s more like… sometimes when people at the museum are talking to me about the next art walk, I’m looking right at them and trying to listen, and then I realize I missed the middle part of what they said. So I’ll have to ask them to run it by me again. It’s a little embarrassing, but it’s not like I can’t understand language, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any decline in your cognitive abilities, such as memory, language, or problem-solving, over the past two years?

I wouldn’t say it’s a big decline exactly… but, yes, I guess it’s been noticeable for a little while. Maybe about two years and a few months—around two years and four months, I’d say. It really started causing trouble after my friend died and I took over the museum liaison duties by myself. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
